cells.tense: Strength is moving outward now, and it reaches people as it is needed.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Settle the heading once, then move, and let the pulls that arrive afterward wait their turn.
cells.core:
Something is entering from outside, and your strength is already heading toward it. This is the shared kind — the strength that leaves you and lands where it is needed, not the kind you hold back. A person, a task, a need you have not yet put words to: what arrives fits what you have to give, and the fit is why it does not empty you.

What to watch is scattering. Strength spread across every open hand thins out and reaches none of them. Turn toward the one direction and stop surveying — one commitment, one heading, named and then walked toward completely, the rest held back for later. Let that heading come from what you want. A flow with a direction runs clean, and the direction is the part that keeps it from running out.
cells.sheetLine: What is arriving matches the strength you have to give.
cells.verb: channeling personal strength into shared resources as they arrive
cells.place: at the threshold where what was outside enters the system

cells.tense: Resources will be flowing before you can see where they are needed.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Meet an arriving need with a fair act, done before anyone can watch you do it — let what feels right decide that case, and skip the tally.
cells.core:
Something is entering and your strength goes out to meet it fast — faster than you can tell what is really wanted yet. Weighing every share before it even arrives has turned support into a ledger, and the people at the other end can feel the scale resting on them. There is more holding than flowing here, and bracing against an arrival you cannot see costs more than the arrival would.

Fairness can move without calculation. Meet one arriving need with a fair act, done where no one will see, and let your own felt sense of what is right make that call rather than the arithmetic. What is coming will still be met, and met well. It just will not be met by you at the door with a set of accounts held up against it.

cells.tense: What was needed went by and you were still at the threshold.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Stay with the hard part of a commitment already made, without adding effort, and see what the pressure tells you is real in it.
cells.core:
Something was coming in, or someone was reaching toward you, and you were back at the door. Not through refusal — some part of the flow toward you stopped arriving, and your strength was held instead of shared. What comes next arrives into a room you have already stepped out of. The trouble is not in what you put out; it is in whether you engage at all.

More generous output is not the repair. Engage one thing on purpose. Stay with the hard part of a commitment already made, and see what the pressure tells you about what is real in it. Show up where the difficulty is and find what holds; what falls away was the method, not the purpose. Release comes after engagement, not in place of it.

cells.tense: The strength moving outward now has a direction you do not claim.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Before a need is met, settle on one direction and stop scanning for others — give toward that one, then let it be done.
cells.core:
You are at the entry point where everything lands, and your strength is going out as things arrive — moved by a hand you do not count as your own. Asked, you would say the circumstances lined up, that people happened to need what you had. What holds is that the outflow has a direction, and that direction was not consciously picked, so it reads as circumstance rather than as something you are doing.

The step back is to the simpler form of the same line: one heading, held or owned, however small. Instead of meeting every need that shows up, take the next one and settle on where it is going before you move toward it. One direction, then the act. Naming the heading puts a hand back on it as the strength goes out.
